cards.title: A runaway supermassive black hole is leaving a cosmic trail of stars
cards.body: Hubble observations revealed an extraordinary cosmic event: a supermassive black hole with roughly twenty million times the mass of the Sun, ejected from its host galaxy. Hurtling through space at over four million kilometers per hour, the rogue giant leaves behind a shock wave in the surrounding intergalactic gas, compressing it and triggering the birth of an unprecedented 200,000-light-year-long trail of new, newborn stars.

sources.title: Hubble Sees Possible Runaway Black Hole Creating a Trail of Stars

cards.title: Solar flares cause planetary-scale magnetic tremors on Mars
cards.body: Unlike Earth, Mars lacks a global protective magnetic field generated by an internal core dynamo. However, data from NASA's MAVEN orbiter and the InSight lander revealed that powerful solar flares trigger global magnetic quakes across Mars. When energetic solar storms slam into the Martian upper atmosphere, induced electric currents drive magnetic disturbances that echo thousands of kilometers down to the planet's very surface.

cards.title: Saturn's tiny moon Mimas hides an ocean beneath its Death Star crater
cards.body: Heavily cratered and seemingly frozen solid, Saturn's moon Mimas looks like the quintessential dead world. Yet subtle wobbles in its orbit, tracked by the Cassini spacecraft, revealed something startling: beneath an icy shell 20 to 30 kilometers thick lies a young global liquid water ocean. Forming just 5 to 15 million years ago, this hidden ocean makes up more than half of Mimas's total interior volume.

cards.title: Supernovae produce cosmic 'cannonball' pulsars traveling at escape velocity
cards.body: When massive stars explode, the blast is rarely symmetrical. The resulting uneven kick can catapult the newborn neutron star across the galaxy at staggering speeds. Pulsar PSR J0002+6216, nicknamed the Cannonball Pulsar, was clocked speeding at over four million kilometers per hour. Moving fast enough to completely escape the Milky Way, it leaves behind a narrow, 13-light-year-long tail of energized gas pointing directly to its birthplace.

sources.title: Astronomers Find 'Cannonball Pulsar' Speeding Through Space

cards.title: Spacecraft can use atmospheric friction to brake into planetary orbit
cards.body: Instead of firing heavy retrorockets and burning tons of propellant to slow down, spacecraft can use 'aerobraking.' By dipping carefully into a planet's wispy upper atmosphere over dozens or hundreds of orbits, a probe lets atmospheric drag bleed off its orbital energy for free. Missions like NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter cut hundreds of kilograms of fuel mass this way, paving the path for larger exploration payloads.

quizzes.question: What is the runaway supermassive black hole creating as it travels through space?
options: A 200,000-light-year-long trail of newborn stars
A giant ring of dark matter
A black hole binary system
A dead void stripped entirely of gas
quizzes.explanation: As the ejected black hole plows through intergalactic gas, it compresses the material, sparking the formation of a vast trail of new stars.

quizzes.question: Why do solar storms induce global magnetic tremors across Mars?
options: Mars lacks a global internal magnetic shield, exposing its atmosphere to solar currents
Mars has an iron core spinning faster than Earth's
Martian dust storms generate massive static electric fields
The Sun pulls Mars closer during solar flares
quizzes.explanation: Because Mars lacks a global dynamo-driven magnetosphere, solar wind currents directly interact with its atmosphere and drive magnetic quakes down to the ground.

quizzes.question: What surprising interior feature was discovered beneath the cratered surface of Mimas?
options: A young global liquid water ocean
A hollow cavity filled with methane gas
A molten iron-nickel core
A massive underground carbon diamond mantle
quizzes.explanation: Despite its heavily cratered exterior, orbital librations detected by Cassini show Mimas harbors a subsurface liquid ocean formed within the past 15 million years.

quizzes.question: How did the 'Cannonball Pulsar' PSR J0002+6216 achieve its extreme velocity?
options: An asymmetric supernova explosion kicked it through space
It was accelerated by a nearby supermassive black hole
Tidal forces from Jupiter pushed it out of orbit
It consumed a white dwarf star's gravitational field
quizzes.explanation: Supernova explosions can be uneven, delivering an immense momentum 'kick' that propels the remnant neutron star at millions of kilometers per hour.

quizzes.question: What is the primary benefit of using aerobraking for planetary probes?
options: It drastically reduces the amount of propellant needed to enter orbit
It cleans space radiation off the probe's solar panels
It recharges the spacecraft's electrical batteries using lightning
It cools down internal computers during planetary approach
quizzes.explanation: Aerobraking converts orbital kinetic energy into atmospheric friction, saving hundreds of kilograms of fuel that would otherwise be required for rocket braking.

guesses.prompt: How long, in light-years, is the trail of newborn stars left behind by the runaway supermassive black hole?
guesses.explanation: The compressed shock trail behind the rogue black hole stretches an astonishing 200,000 light-years—twice the diameter of the Milky Way galaxy.

guesses.prompt: Roughly how many millions of years old is the subsurface ocean of Saturn's moon Mimas?
guesses.explanation: Astronomers estimate the hidden ocean inside Mimas formed exceptionally recently in cosmic terms, between just 5 and 15 million years ago.

misconceptions.claim: Heavily cratered, geologically inactive-looking moons cannot harbor liquid water oceans.
misconceptions.explanation: Even though Mimas shows no geysers or fractured crust like Europa or Enceladus, orbital measurements prove it hides a massive global liquid water ocean.

misconceptions.claim: Entering orbit around a planet always requires firing large rocket thrusters to slow down.
misconceptions.explanation: Through aerobraking, missions can gently graze a planet's upper atmosphere over multiple passes, letting air resistance do the heavy deceleration work.
